newsitem.title: POLAND: Hungary, Poland should avoid Czech crisis - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Hungary, Poland should avoid Czech crisis - JP Morgan.

text.p: Hungary and Poland are likely to avoid a crisis similar to that in the Czech Republic and any spillover effects from turmoil on Czech markets should be short-term, a JP Morgan report published on May 30 said.
"Different fundamentals in Hungary and Poland suggest that the immediate spillover effects from the Czech crisis will not be long-lasting," the Data Watch publication said.
It said Hungary had implemented a stabilisation programme to improve its trade balance, which had resulted in lower trade deficits over the last two years.
It said Polish policymakers had to keep control over a rapidly growing trade gap, which grew more in the first quarter than in all of 1996, even at the cost of slower economic growth.
"(Polish) policymakers will have to ensure that this (trade balance) deterioration does not get out of control, and hence growth may have to slow from its current rapid pace," it said.
Poland's gross domestic product grew six percent in 1996 and nearly eight percent in the first quarter of this year, according to some think-tanks.
